newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Soyuz and Mir get ready to dock.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Soyuz and Mir get ready to dock.

text.p: The relief crew aboard the Soyuz spacecraft and the tired three-man team on the troubled Mir space station were just 250 metres (yards) from each other at around 1645 GMT on Thursday and ready for docking.
Radio conversations between the two crews and Mission Control outside Moscow centred on communications details and none of the cosmonauts showed any sign of tension.
Experts at Mission Control, where the main hall was packed with Russian experts and representatives from NASA and the European Space Agency, were tense but there was no sign of last minute trouble.
"The two crews are ready for docking," a Mission Control operator announced.

Mir suffered its worst accident on June 25, when a supply ship pierced its Spektr scientific module during a manual docking manoeuvre. Cosmonauts had to unplug power cables leading from Spektr's solar panels as they fled the module and sealed it. The accident deprived Mir of up to half of its power supply.

Mission Control had planned for the current crew to carry out the repairs but changed its mind and effectively stood them down after a series of other accidents and a stress-imposed heart problem developed by commander Vasily Tsibliyev.
Mir and Soyuz are scheduled to dock at around 1703 GMT.

Relief crew commander Anatoly Solovyov, 49, and 43-year-old flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov are to meet the current three-men crew at about 1830 GMT when the hatch between Mir and Soyuz is due to be opened.
The new crew face a daunting task of trying to restore power to the ageing station.
Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin are scheduled to return to Earth on August 14. British-American physicist Michael Foale will remain on board until late September.
